questions.knowledge_point: Transforming a 2x2 Matrix Into the Identity Matrix Using Row Operations
questions.problem:
Which of the following matrices are transformed into the $2\times 2$ identity matrix after applying the row operations ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{2},\,$ ${R}_{1}:=4{R}_{1},\,$ and $\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1}?$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ \frac{1}{4} & 0\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ \frac{1}{4} & 0\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ \frac{3}{4} & 0\end{aligned}]
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's apply the operations to each of the matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ \frac{1}{4} & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4} & 0 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne I\,\times  \\ B & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ \frac{1}{4} & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4} & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =I\,✓ \\ C & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ \frac{3}{4} & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4} & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ -5 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne I\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$B$ only".

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying the Inverse of a 2x2 Matrix Calculated Using Row Operations
questions.problem:
The inverse of the $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine ${A}^{-1}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & -5 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 &  &  \\ 0 & 1 &  & \end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We write down $A$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $A$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & -5 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-3){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -5 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix ${A}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{A}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}-5 & -3 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

$$

\begin{aligned}[Y\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{3}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & \frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We write down $Y$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $Y$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[Y\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{3}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{2}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & \frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding row operations are

$$
{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1},\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1},\,{R}_{2}:=-\frac{2}{3}{R}_{2},\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{2}.
$$

The matrix ${Y}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{Y}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3} \\ -\frac{1}{3} & -\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}].
$$
